import numpy as np
from PIL import Image

def clahe(gray, tiles=8, clip=3.0):
    img = gray.astype(np.float32)
    h,w = img.shape
    th, tw = h//tiles, w//tiles
    maps = np.zeros((tiles,tiles,256), np.float32)
    for i in range(tiles):
        for j in range(tiles):
            tile = img[i*th:(i+1)*th, j*tw:(j+1)*tw]
            hist,_ = np.histogram(tile, bins=256, range=(0,255))
            # clip
            limit = clip*tile.size/256
            excess = np.maximum(hist-limit,0).sum()
            hist = np.minimum(hist,limit)
            hist += excess/256
            cdf = np.cumsum(hist); cdf/=cdf[-1]
            maps[i,j]=cdf*255
    out = np.zeros_like(img)
    # bilinear interpolation of tile maps
    for y in range(h):
        fy = (y/th)-0.5
        i0 = int(np.floor(fy)); i1=i0+1
        wy = fy-i0
        i0c=min(max(i0,0),tiles-1); i1c=min(max(i1,0),tiles-1)
        for x in range(w):
            fx=(x/tw)-0.5
            j0=int(np.floor(fx)); j1=j0+1
            wx=fx-j0
            j0c=min(max(j0,0),tiles-1); j1c=min(max(j1,0),tiles-1)
            v=int(img[y,x])
            top=maps[i0c,j0c,v]*(1-wx)+maps[i0c,j1c,v]*wx
            bot=maps[i1c,j0c,v]*(1-wx)+maps[i1c,j1c,v]*wx
            out[y,x]=top*(1-wy)+bot*wy
    return np.clip(out,0,255).astype(np.uint8)
